title: When the Debt Breaks
premise: Edmund Kavanagh, a crash investigator whose wife and daughter died in row twelve of Flight 4471, has spent three years assigning blame to paperwork no one reads. When a burner phone recovered from a wreck site rings with her daughter's recorded voice, she discovers the crash was engineered by Meridian Debt Holdings to erase whistleblowers — and the same firm is scheduling a second 'accident' against a train carrying debt-forgiveness activists. Aided by a disgraced actuary and the hacker who built the burner network, Edmund races to expose the kill-list before the attack, ultimately forcing a confession mid-broadcast and choosing found family over vengeance when she has the architect of row twelve at her mercy.
about_author: Juniper Okonkwo is a former insurance fraud analyst who left the industry after a case she can't talk about. She writes thrillers about ordinary people who discover the machinery behind their grief.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Three years after losing her family on Flight 4471, Edmund works a thankless rural crash site, cataloging debris with clinical detachment. Finding an intact burner phone in the wreckage unsettles her; burners don't survive fires like this. Emotional beat: grief armored in procedure, cracked by one impossible object.

chapters.title: The Number That Calls Back
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. At home, the burner rings. The voice is her daughter's — a synthesized splice from old voicemails — reciting coordinates and the word 'Meridian.' She reports it and is told the phone isn't in any evidence log. Beat: terror braided with hope, the cruelest combination.

chapters.title: Chain of Custody
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. She pulls the flight's final maintenance records and finds pages replaced with clean forgeries — her specialty is spotting exactly this. Her supervisor warns her off, gently, which frightens her more than hostility would. Beat: the institution she trusted becomes a suspect.

chapters.title: The Actuary Who Quit
chapters.summary: Delphine Okafor's POV. Delphine, who priced risk for Meridian Debt Holdings until she saw a 'contingent liability' column that was actually a kill-list, recognizes Edmund's name from leaked files. She contacts her through the burner's own network. Beat: two damaged women circling trust.

chapters.title: What the Numbers Weighed
chapters.summary: Delphine's POV. Delphine shows Edmund the actuarial model: Flight 4471 was written as a $40 million saving against lawsuits. Row twelve held every whistleblower. Edmund realizes her family was collateral, not targets — worse, somehow. Beat: rage crystallizing into purpose.

chapters.title: Ghost Protocol, Cheap Version
chapters.summary: Tomas Reyes' POV. Tomas, the hacker who built the burner relay for a dead friend inside Meridian, explains the phone only calls people on the next kill-list. It called Edmund by mistake — or so he thinks. Beat: paranoid camaraderie, dark humor as armor.

chapters.title: The Second List
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Decrypted files reveal a scheduled event: a regional train carrying debt-relief organizers, coded as 'recourse.' Date: eleven days out. Edmund goes to the NTSB and is stonewalled by someone reading from prepared language. Beat: dread with a countdown attached.

chapters.title: Prepared Language
chapters.summary: Deputy Director Hale's POV. Hale, pressured from above, genuinely believes Edmund is a grieving conspiracy theorist — until he cross-checks one forged signature and finds his own name authorized it. Beat: complicity discovered too late to be innocent.

chapters.title: Eleven Days
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. The team holes up in Tomas's shuttered arcade: Delphine modeling the attack's financial logic, Tomas tracing the relay, Edmund reconstructing 4471's final minutes. They argue, eat bad takeout, become something like a unit. Beat: found family forming under pressure.

chapters.title: A Man Named Voss
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Meridian's 'risk solutions' director learns the burner survived and dispatches cleaners. He's not a monster in his own mind; he's a man balancing books. He orders Edmund followed, not killed — yet. Beat: banal evil, patient and polite.

chapters.title: Tail Lights
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Edmund spots the surveillance tail and deliberately leads them to her family's graves, turning grief into theater while photographing the operatives' plates. One plate traces to a private security firm owned by Meridian. Beat: grief weaponized.

chapters.title: The Relay Farm
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Tomas finds the physical server barn broadcasting the daughter's voice and realizes the messages were generated live — someone inside Meridian is feeding them intel. He doesn't tell the others yet. Beat: suspicion planted inside the found family.

chapters.title: Eight Days
chapters.summary: Delphine's POV. Delphine identifies the attack mechanism: a maintenance override sold to the rail operator as a cost-saving patch. Proving it requires the patch's sign-off — held by the man who signed 4471's forged logs. Beat: the conspiracy has one spine.

chapters.title: The Man Who Signed Twice
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Edmund confronts engineer Peter Lassiter, who signed both documents. He confesses in a parking garage, terrified, then begs protection. Before she can move him, a cleaner's car arrives. Beat: witness gained, clock accelerated.

chapters.title: Running Lassiter
chapters.summary: Hale's POV. Hale, now quietly rogue himself, shelters Lassiter in an NTSB safe house and feeds Edmund what he can. Voss's team closes in. Beat: institutional redemption, bought at personal ruin.

chapters.title: Six Days
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. The mole inside their group surfaces: Tomas admits he took money from Meridian months ago to keep the relay alive — before he knew what it carried. Delphine nearly walks. Edmund holds them together with the truth instead of forgiveness. Beat: fracture and repair.

chapters.title: The Voice Is Not Hers
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Edmund finally listens past her daughter's voice in the recordings and hears the handler beneath it — Voss himself, taunting her personally. This was never a mistake; she was recruited as leverage against Hale. Beat: manipulation revealed, fury refined into clarity.

chapters.title: Four Days
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs interwoven. The plan assembles: Delphine will trigger Meridian's own audit flags, Tomas will hijack the relay broadcast, Hale will arrest Lassiter's handlers, Edmund will board the train. Everyone names what they're afraid of losing. Beat: quiet before the storm, vows exchanged.

chapters.title: Recourse
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Day of the attack. Edmund rides the targeted train while remotely walking a dispatcher through overriding the sabotage patch. The train slows through the kill zone as Voss's failsafe triggers early. Beat: white-knuckle climax, competence as love.

chapters.title: The Confession Engine
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Tomas broadcasts Voss's own voice-printed instructions and the kill-list across every Meridian terminal simultaneously. Executives scramble, deny, and begin selling each other out within the hour. Beat: the machine turned on its makers.

chapters.title: What Edmund Was Owed
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Edmund finds Voss before the arrests do, alone, with the means for violence in reach. He offers her the thing she wants: acknowledgment that row twelve was murder. She takes the recording, not the revenge, and lets the law have him. Beat: justice chosen over vengeance, at real cost.

chapters.title: After the Wreckage
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Months later: hearings, indictments, Hale testifying. Edmund, Delphine, and Tomas share an unremarkable dinner — the burner phone silent in a drawer, kept not as a wound but as proof she answered. Beat: belonging earned, grief carried together.
